CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioners - husband and his family members are before this Court calling in question proceedings in S.C.No.10036/2022, pending before the V Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Tumakuru (Sitting at Tiptur), for the offences under Sections 498A and 313 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text:
Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Tumakuru (Sitting at Tiptur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2, in unison submit that the parties to the lis were before the family Court in M.C.No.6/2021 and the concerned family Court has passed the judgment on 05.09.2023 granting decree of divorce in the aforesaid petition.
Now the couple have parted their way after obtaining the decree of divorce.

It is NC: 2024:KHC:32072 also their submission that during the pendency of this petition, the parties have settled the dispute amicably among themselves and respondent No.2 on her own will has agreed to withdraw the impugned proceedings.
An application under Section 320(2) of the Cr.P.C. along with joint memo and an affidavit is filed before this Court to that effect.

3. The joint memo filed by the petitioners and respondent No.2 reads as follows:
".... .... ....
3. Further as per the Examination of RW1 the second respondent has agreed to withdraw / quashing the said Criminal Case.

Under these circumstances the petitioners prefer this criminal petition for quashing the FIR, Complaint & charge sheet & entire proceedings in SC No.10036/2022 on the file of V Additional District & Sessions Court at Tumkur sitting at Tiptur as per Annexure - F.
4.

entities.text: Additional District & Sessions Court at Tumkur sitting at Tiptur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: IN view of the settlement arrived at, the complainant / respondent No.2 has no wish to continue the criminal proceedings initiated by her and she has given up all the allegations no.2 has no objection for quashing the criminal proceedings pending against the petitioners.

5. The petitioners and the complainant / respondent no.2 have understood the contents of the joint memo and out of their free will, volition and without any fear, force, threat or coercion, have affixed their signature to this joint memo."
NC: 2024:KHC:32072

In the light of the fact that the parties have already parted their ways and arrived at settlement and as it is a marital dispute, I deem it appropriate to accept the application,
joint memo and the affidavit and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are not against the State.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
